page: Amazon Web Services c6g.8xlarge is a compute-optimized instance powered by the AWS Nitro hypervisor and custom ARMv8-based AWS Graviton2 processors. It features 32 dedicated physical cores running at 2.5 GHz with a 1:1 thread-to-core ratio, meaning hyperthreading is disabled. The instance is equipped with 64.0 GB of memory, providing 2.0 GB of RAM per core. It lacks local storage and dedicated GPU hardware, relying entirely on network-attached storage and baseline network bandwidth of 12 Gbps.

In benchmark evaluations, the c6g.8xlarge demonstrates moderate compute capabilities. The stress-ng single-core and multi-core CPU performance tests place the instance in the average tier, with scores of 1519.19 and 48574.31 respectively. Geekbench multi-core performance and software compilation with Clang also rank in the average tier. However, single-threaded operations show some limitations, with Geekbench single-core, single-threaded gzip compression, and single-threaded bzip3 decompression falling into the weak tier.

The instance's memory subsystem registers an average read-only small block bandwidth of 1894.03 GB/sec, though the PassMark memory score is classified as weak. Database operations perform in the average tier, with Redis SET operations reaching 38.64 million operations per second and PassMark database operations scoring 20293.24. Static web serving throughput is measured at 33.12 GB/sec. Given these characteristics, the c6g.8xlarge is suitable for multi-threaded workloads such as web serving, software compilation, and moderate database operations, while being less optimal for single-threaded tasks or memory-intensive applications.
description: Amazon Web Services c6g.8xlarge is an arm64 compute-optimized instance featuring 32 dedicated physical cores powered by AWS Graviton Neoverse-N1 processors running at 2.5 GHz. It is configured with 64.0 GB of memory, yielding 2.0 GB per core, and operates on the AWS Nitro hypervisor. The instance lacks local storage and GPUs, but provides a baseline network bandwidth of 12 Gbps. Benchmark data shows average multi-core CPU performance, with a stress-ng multi-core score of 48574.31 and a Geekbench multi-core score of 11649.0. However, single-threaded performance is weak, as evidenced by a Geekbench single-core score of 958.0 and lower single-threaded compression speeds. Database and web serving capabilities are average, with Redis SET operations achieving 38.64 million operations per second. This instance is best suited for multi-threaded workloads, software compilation, and static web serving.
